newsitem.title: USA: SEC clears curbs on telemarketing of muni bonds.
newsitem.headline: SEC clears curbs on telemarketing of muni bonds.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission approved a rule barring municipal bond brokers and dealers from making abusive telephone marketing calls to investors.

Rule G-39, which was tentatively approved by the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board in August, generally bars broker-dealers from making "cold call" sales to muni bond investors before 800 EST and after 2100 EST, unless dealers get prior consent from investors.
Dealers also must keep a no cold-call list of investors who, when called the first time, said they did not wish to be contacted again.

The rule implements a telemarketing law enacted by the U.S. Congress over two years ago. SEC is in the process of approving similar rules by self-regulatory organizations (SROs) for other sectors of the securities markets.

The new MSRB rule requires broker-dealers that do telephone sales between 800 EST and 2100 EST to disclose, in a clear manner, their names, their firms' names, and the address and telephone number where they can be contacted.
They also must make clear that the purpose of the call is to sell securities.
